captionLines: The People of the State of New York, Respondent, v Jamel Walston, Appellant.

qualifierLines: {**23 NY3d at 988} OPINION OF THE COURT

I join the Court's memorandum opinion, which follows our case law in holding that an O'Rama error is a mode of proceedings error when a trial judge fails to disclose to counsel the full contents of a jury note. I add this concurring opinion to suggest that we should be willing to{**23 NY3d at 991} consider in the future an argument, not made here, that the cases so holding, including People v O'Rama (78 NY2d 270, 279 [1991]) itself to the extent that it finds a mode of proceedings error, should be overruled. This idea finds support in some of our more recent jury note cases, which have taken a flexible approach to the mode of proceedings doctrine, and which may be read as eroding O'Rama's force as precedent (, 21 NY3d 932 [2013]; , 15 NY3d 824 [2010]).
